group: two-counter doubling map, halting on an exact remainder
title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1LC---_1LE1RD_1RA0RC_0LF0LA_0LD0RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1LC---_1LE1RD_1RA0RC_0LF0LA_0LD0RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and Collatz-like. Each time the head turns at the left end the tape is 1n (01)k 111 (or all ones), and the next such state is given by an explicit map on (state, n, k): while n is odd the ones are doubled at the cost of (n+5)/2 pairs 01, or the pairs are doubled when that cannot be paid; when n is even the pairs are drained into ones. The machine halts if and only if a doubling in state D leaves exactly one pair, that is the orbit reaches D(n, k) with n odd and 2k = n+7 (as far as the computed map is right: it is checked against the machine on thousands of states, not proved). From blank tape the map has been iterated through 8,598 epochs, more than 103,100 steps, without a halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 24,444 cells have been visited and 15,911 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.433). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.09).

claims.title: The drain
claims.text: From the left end, A> 0 0 12n+4 (01)k+2 111 becomes A> 0 0 12n+12 (01)k 111 in 12n+58 steps: each trip turns one 01 into four 1s.

claims.title: How a halt happens
claims.text: A sweep in state D over an even block of 1s that ends in 0 111 reaches B on a 1 (no transition) in 2n+3 steps, whatever lies to the right; over an odd block ending in 0 1111 it passes to the right end.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>300</sup> steps
claims.text: py/run.py (exact run-length simulation, cycles extrapolated at the turns of the head, nested loops level by level) follows 414 epochs from blank tape to 10300 steps without a halt. The extrapolation agrees with the plain run-length simulator at all 8,828 samples up to 3·108 steps, and the epoch map agrees with bbtools.machine on the values tried.

claims.title: The left-end map
claims.text: With A(n, k), D(n, k) the head in state A two cells (D: three cells) left of 1n (01)k 111 (k = 0: 1n): for n even, s(n, k) → other(n+4, k−1), and other(n+7, 0) when k = 1, other(n+3, 0) when k = 0; A(n, 0) → D(1, (n+1)/2) and D(n, 0) → D(3, (n+1)/2) for n odd; for n odd and k ≥ 2: D(n, k) → D(2n+7, k−(n+5)/2) and A(n, k) → A(2n+6, k−(n+5)/2) when 2k > n+5, all ones of length 2n+10 resp. 2n+9 when 2k = n+5, other(n−2k+6, 2k) when 2k < n+5; n odd and k = 1 halts. Equal to the plain machine on all 7,000 states with n < 70, k < 50, 300 random larger states, the first 170 left-end states from blank tape and every epoch N ≤ 150; its epoch values agree with the 126 epochs of the accelerated run to 10100 steps. Checked, not proved.

claims.title: The halting condition
claims.text: By the map, the machine halts iff the orbit from D(3, 0) reaches D(n, k) with n odd and 2k = n+7: the doubling leaves one pair, D(2n+7, 1), and the machine stops within the next sweeps (the Lean lemma halt_even shows the kind of sweep that stops it). A doubling in A leaves n even and a failed doubling leaves k even, so there is no other way.

claims.title: No halt in 8,598 epochs
claims.text: The map iterated from D(3, 0) for 9.1·10<sup>7</sup> map steps (a run of drain steps counted once) does not halt; the last all-ones tape has a length of 10,317 bits, so the machine has made more than 10<sup>3,100</sup> steps. This rests on the computed map.

claims.title: A halt needs an exact remainder
claims.text: Each doubling stage in D ends with a remainder between 0 and about n/2, and a halt needs it to be exactly 1: about 2/n per stage if remainders behave like random numbers, with n growing geometrically. Past the epochs already followed the chance is around 2<sup>−10,000</sup>.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It is the question whether the orbit of the left-end map ever reaches D(n, (n+7)/2) with n odd: a Collatz-like question. The map and this reduction are computed, not yet proved in Lean (the doubling stage, a nested zig-zag, is the missing part).

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB---_1RC1LE_0RD0RF_0RE0LA_1LF0LB_1LA1LD up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet, and it looks like a Collatz problem. The tape is a block of ones followed by a block of 01s, and the machine keeps trading one for the other: doubling the ones, paying in 01s, then draining the 01s back into ones. It stops only if a doubling leaves exactly one 01. In 8,598 epochs (more than 10<sup>3,100</sup> steps) that has not happened.

facts.text: The only way it can stop, proved in Lean.
The halting condition on the left-end map (computed, checked against the machine).
No halt along the orbit of the map: more than 10<sup>3,100</sup> steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.433). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.09).
After 109 steps the tape spans 24,444 cells (16,450 left of the start, 167 right), with a density of 1s of 0.651.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Ones, then 01s: a map on two numbers
html: Each time the head turns at the left end the tape is 1n (01)k 111, or all ones. Write A(n, k) or D(n, k) for that tape with the head in state A or D. The next left-end state is:

stateconditionnext
all ones, n oddD(1, (n+1)/2) from A, D(3, (n+1)/2) from Dconversion
all ones, n evenother(n+3, 0)
n evenk ≥ 2other(n+4, k−1)drain
n evenk = 1other(n+7, 0)all ones again
n odd2k > n+5D(2n+7, k−(n+5)/2) or A(2n+6, k−(n+5)/2)doubling
n odd2k = n+5all ones: D(2n+10, 0) or A(2n+9, 0)
n odd2 ≤ k, 2k < n+5other(n−2k+6, 2k)failed doubling
n oddk = 1halt

(“other” is the other letter.) From blank tape: D(3,0) → D(3,2) → A(5,4) → D(3,8) → D(13,4) → A(11,8) → A(31,0) → D(1,16) → D(9,13) → D(25,6) → A(19,12) → A(47,0) → … The all-ones states D(N, 0) are the epochs: N = 3, 124, 583, 2143, 8167, 34679, …, growing by a factor 2.3 on average. An epoch takes about N2 steps, which is why the tape grows like the square root of the step count.
The map was found from the run and is checked against the plain machine on more than 7,000 built tapes and on the run from blank tape; it is not yet proved in Lean (only the drain is).

sections.heading: Only if a doubling leaves exactly one 01
html: The only halt is state B reading 1; Lean proves the kind of sweep that does it: state D over an even block of ones that ends in 0 111. On the map the halt comes from a state with n odd and k = 1, and it can only come from a doubling in D: D(n, k) with 2k = n+7 goes to D(2n+7, 1) and stops. (A doubling in A leaves n even; a failed doubling leaves k even.) For example the tape of 26 ones halts: D(26,0) → A(29,0) → D(1,15) → D(9,12) → D(25,5) → A(21,10) → D(7,20) → D(21,14) → D(49,1) → halt.

From blank tape the map has been followed through 8,598 epochs, more than 103,100 steps, and 2k = n+7 never occurred in state D. Each doubling stage leaves a remainder that looks random between 0 and n/2, so the chance of hitting exactly 1 shrinks like 2/n while n grows geometrically: the machine almost certainly never halts. Proving it would mean controlling exact remainders along an exponentially growing orbit, as for the Collatz-like cryptids.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: At the left end the tape is 1^n (01)^k 111; the next left-end state is an explicit map on (state, n, k): doubling n at the cost of (n+5)/2 pairs, draining pairs into ones. It halts iff a doubling in state D leaves exactly one pair (2k = n+7). Map computed and checked; no halt in 8,598 epochs (> 10^3,100 steps).
